item.title: If I change this default, what else is going to change?
item.content:encoded: A setting's current value does not tell you whether it will follow the default, preserve an exception or obey a policy.

item.title: If you remove a control, who has to make the decision now?
item.content:encoded: Removing a control doesn't remove the work. Yoto shows where settings belong and what the person using the product still needs to see.

item.title: There's more to do before you ask 'Are you sure?'
item.content:encoded: Before adding 'Are you sure?', work out what the person still needs to choose, check or try.

item.title: The system broke it. Why is the user fixing it?
item.content:encoded: Products are good at detecting failure. They're often much worse at making clear who can actually fix it.

item.title: When a redesign makes familiar work slower
item.content:encoded: A cleaner redesign can still be a worse tool for the people who know it best.

item.title: Stop turning every answer into text
item.content:encoded: AI can answer the question and still make the user do the work of turning it into something useful.

item.title: Remember the work, not just the user
item.content:encoded: Remembering a login is easy. Remembering what someone was trying to finish is where the product promise starts.

item.title: Your product is making people wait in the dark
item.content:encoded: A waiting state should tell someone what is happening, what they can safely do next, and what happens if nothing changes.

item.title: Your churn survey might be lying to you
item.content:encoded: A churn reason is not clean evidence if the cancellation flow shaped the answer before the user gave it.
